I've been farming this land for 20 years. I know Quzhou's soil — sandy loam, not too deep, and the wells have been dropping a bit each year, so I can't waste water. My wife and two kids help during busy season, but labor is tight. Here's how I'm thinking through this year.

**Wheat and Maize (same 20 mu, double cropped):** I always do wheat-maize rotation on my best flat parcels. Winter wheat goes in October, I harvest it in June, then immediately plant summer maize on the same ground. This land works hardest. For wheat I use the improved Jimai series — everyone around here uses it, proven yield. Maize I use hybrid seed,郑单958 type. I'll rotary till before wheat, then no-till into wheat stubble for maize to save time and moisture.

**Cotton (10 mu):** Cotton is hard work but the price has been decent. I plant Bt cotton — cuts down on pesticide costs compared to what my father used to spray. I'll deep plough this plot in early spring before planting. Cotton needs the most pesticide attention even with Bt varieties, especially for aphids and bollworm later in season.

**Stevia (28.1 mu):** This is my main cash crop now. I have a procurement contract with a processing company. Stevia takes up my largest area. I'll plant seedlings in late April after last frost, then harvest leaves two or three times through the season before frost hits again in October. Rotary till before transplanting. Steady irrigation is critical — stevia doesn't like drought stress between harvests.

For irrigation, I'm careful. The well costs electricity money and groundwater is everyone's concern here. I irrigate strategically at critical growth stages, not on a fixed schedule.
